data.gender_notes: Debarati is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Debarati is a Sanskrit name derived from the words ‘Deba’ meaning God and ‘Rati’ meaning the beloved or wife of a god. This name is associated with Goddess Durga, the warrior goddess who is the mother of the universe and the wife of Lord Shiva. Debarati represents the divine feminine energy, strength, and devotion. The name Debarati carries the meaning “Goddess Durga's beloved” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Debarati usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess durga's beloved and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Debarati belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess Durga's beloved.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Debarati total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

She was a prominent leader who played a crucial role in organizing protests, strikes, and civil disobedience campaigns against the British rule. Debarati Chattopadhyay was also known for her fiery speeches and her dedication towards the cause of Indian independence.

historical_references.reference: Debarati Gupta, a renowned archaeologist and epigraphist, was born on 20 August 1912 in the village of Khatra in present-day Bangladesh. She studied Sanskrit and Epigraphy at the University of Calcutta and then went on to study at the School of Oriental and African Studies in London. Debarati Gupta made significant contributions to the field of Indian archaeology, particularly in the areas of Brahmi and Sharda scripts. Her most famous work is the 'Corpus of Epigraphic Inscriptions of India and Pakistan', which is considered a standard reference work for scholars and researchers.
